subject.title: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs in cron config

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public restart catch-up policy for cron jobs, and should the supported opt-out skip missed runs or only defer them?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but this adds public config and changes scheduler restart semantics; the existing internal knobs do not directly implement the reporter's zero-means-skip expectation.

options.title: Define explicit catch-up policy
options.body: Add a documented global policy, and possibly a later per-job override, where current catch-up remains the default and skip/disable/stagger semantics are explicit and tested.

options.title: Expose raw internal knobs
options.body: Expose `maxMissedJobsPerRestart` and `missedJobStaggerMs` directly, but document that zero defers all missed jobs or intentionally special-case zero to skip with tests.

options.title: Keep controls internal
options.body: Keep the fixed internal restart catch-up defaults and document the current behavior/workarounds instead of expanding public cron config.

recommendation.title: Define explicit catch-up policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented global policy, and possibly a later per-job override, where current catch-up remains the default and skip/disable/stagger semantics are explicit and tested.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a compatibility-sensitive public config and scheduler-semantics decision, and steipete landed the original internal catch-up behavior and adjacent cron config/storage work.
